content: Common community pattern for BigInt-based subnet calculators: parse address into a single BigInt (32-bit for IPv4, 128-bit for IPv6) by concatenating shifted octet/hextet values, build a prefix mask as ((1n << 128n) - 1n) ^ ((1n << (128n - prefixLen)) - 1n) (or equivalent all-ones-then-shift), AND the address with the mask for network address, OR with the inverted mask for broadcast/last address. IPv6 has no broadcast address concept -- multicast replaces it, and 'last address' is simply the top of the range, not a reserved special address. This is third-party blog/tool-vendor content, not a spec -- treat as illustrative pattern, not authoritative.
